subject: Geo handoff, subprocessor list, and retention/deletion handoff — BrightBank Q&A
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex@brightbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: where are requests processed / who are your subprocessors?

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — product looked solid. Before we kick off a short pilot, InfoSec asked for a concise summary of where BrightBank customer requests are processed, which subprocessors might touch data, and any potential cross-border hops we should account for. High-level is fine, plus any attachments you can share.

Their main asks:
- Primary regions (where inference runs)
- Known subprocessors (compute, logging, monitoring)
- Any cases where data leaves the US (e.g., for batch jobs, fallback routing, or vendor analytics)
- Retention and deletion commitments for customer request logs and prompt history

Can you send something we can share internally (and with our procurement/security folks)?

Appreciate it —
Alex
Alex Romero
Head of Security, BrightBank
alex@brightbank.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where are requests processed / who are your subprocessors?

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (who owns partner/subprocessor inventory) and Ben (solutions eng) so we can provide a short packet you can share with InfoSec and procurement.

We’ll assemble: a one-page processing map, a CSV of subprocessors we expect to touch production requests, and a short note on cross-border fallback behavior and deletion timelines.

Expect a concise packet from us by Monday COB. Quick note up front: for hosted customers, inference runs primarily in the US (us-west/us-east), and we offer EU-only execution for customers who require it via Private or Dedicated deployments. We’ll include specific provider names and regions in the packet.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@brightbank.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Processing packet and attachments (BrightBank)

Alex — attaching the packet we discussed. Contents:

1) redwood-residency-map-aug2026.pdf — a simplified diagram showing: primary serving regions (us-west-2, us-east-1), optional EU execution (eu-west-1), and fallback routing rules.
2) subprocessor-inventory-aug2026.csv — current list of third-party providers that may handle logs/metrics/ingestion during processing windows.
3) Short FAQ in the PDF that answers common procurement questions.

Quick highlights (TL;DR):
- Primary execution: requests are executed in the customer-configured region. For BrightBank on hosted plan: default is US regions (us-west-2 or us-east-1) depending on routing and latency.
- Subprocessors: compute infra (public cloud provider), object storage for logs (encrypted buckets), telemetry/metrics provider, and optional model vendor for curated models. Names and datapaths are in the CSV.
- Cross-border: automated cross-border transfers are not performed for customer request payloads under normal operation. Exceptions: scheduled analytics jobs (aggregate telemetry) and failover routing may route to an alternate region; such flows are noted and require approval in contract.
- Retention & deletion: customer request metadata and prompt history retention defaults to 30 days (configurable). Complete deletion of request-related data and cached KV entries occurs within 30 days after a termination or explicit deletion request; we provide an export and a deletion confirmation report.

Attachments: redwood-residency-map-aug2026.pdf (PDF), subprocessor-inventory-aug2026.csv (CSV)

Let us know if you want us to redact provider-level names before you share with broader panels — happy to provide a redacted version for procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Partner Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Romero <alex@brightbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Processing packet and attachments (BrightBank)

Marissa / Mina — thanks for the fast turn. A couple quick clarifications from InfoSec before we start an NDA review:

1) When you say "fallback routing may route to an alternate region," can you confirm whether any plaintext customer prompts or model input can ever leave the US in fallback?
2) For the 30-day deletion window: is there an SLA for deletion confirmation and an option for expedited deletion (e.g., 7 days) as part of contract negotiations?
3) Can you confirm whether any subprocessor in the CSV is based in an APAC country and whether that vendor may access unredacted request logs?

If you can reply with short, shareable bullets we can attach to our vendor review doc that would be ideal.

— Alex
Alex Romero
Head of Security, BrightBank
alex@brightbank.com
